Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Q1 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Monica Desai, Investor Relations Manager. Please go ahead.

Monica Desai, Investor Relations Manager:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to StellarTech’s Q1 earnings call. With me today are Alan Reynolds, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; David Lee, COO; and Emily Carter, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our press release and earnings slides, which are available on our IR website. Please note that this call may contain forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Alan Reynolds.

Alan Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Monica, and welcome, everyone.

We had a strong quarter with performance driven by several key initiatives. First, I’d like to discuss our sales guidance for the next few quarters and the full year. Building upon our provided guidance of $11.5 billion to $12.5 billion for Q2, we anticipate sequential revenue growth throughout the year, significantly driven by the burgeoning AI demand across our AetherCloud, NexusConnect, and QuantumEdge segments, which reflects our continued execution on core growth priorities.

We also made meaningful progress with our customer LTA update with ARM Holdings, and would like to offer an update on the underutilization charges for this quarter. This agreement signifies a substantial deepening of our strategic partnership and underscores our commitment to supporting ARM's next-generation technology roadmap.

On a broader level, the first quarter revenue results, which outperformed our initial guidance, supported our positioning. We landed at a strong $11.7 billion, a figure that significantly outperformed our initial guidance. This result represents a 6% increase compared to the $11.04 billion reported in the fourth quarter of 2023 and a 9% increase year-over-year compared to the $10.73 billion recorded in the first quarter of 2023.

I’ll now hand it over to Sarah Chen to walk you through the financials.

Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Alan, and hello, everyone.

This quarter’s financial results were underpinned by operational rigor and discipline. Let’s walk through the key metrics.

To start, the Q2 P&L guidance, specifically regarding revenue and gross margin, helped drive improvements in our financial outlook. We anticipate Q2 2024 revenue to fall within a range of $1.85 billion to $1.95 billion, with a midpoint of $1.9 billion.

Additionally, the net margin and Diluted EPS (earnings per share) results showed strong potential. While we reported a negative Diluted EPS of -$0.04 for the quarter, this represents a significant outperformance against our initial guidance of -$0.15.

Finally, operating margin results for Q2, including QoQ and YoY changes with reasons, and how they compare to our guidance from last quarter, are all positive. In Q2, we achieved an operating margin of 18.5%, a significant improvement compared to both Q1 and the same period last year.

Now I’ll pass it to David Lee to provide color on execution.

David Lee, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

From a delivery and operations standpoint, this was one of our more efficient quarters in recent memory.

A big part of that was our customer LTA update with ARM Holdings, and our update on the underutilization charges for this quarter, which allowed us to secure a specific percentage of our advanced node capacity for ARM’s silicon designs, ensuring they have prioritized access to our leading-edge manufacturing capabilities, specifically targeting 3nm and potentially beyond.

We also saw execution gains related to the net margin and Diluted EPS results, including automation of manufacturing processes, streamlined supply chain management, and consolidation of office space.

Lastly, we began pilots tied to CapEx, and the CapEx comments for this quarter, where early signs are promising. Our net CapEx for Q1 2023 landed at $7 billion. This figure reflects significant investments across our core business units, strategic infrastructure upgrades, and initial expansion efforts related to our emerging IFS initiatives.

Now I’ll turn it over to Emily Carter to discuss technology.

Emily Carter, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, David.

On the technology side, our teams delivered important milestones across multiple streams.

First, we completed major feature work aligned with the customer LTA update with ARM Holdings, especially the technology collaboration and co-development, facilitating deeper technical collaboration between our engineering teams and ARM's silicon architects.

We also rolled out enhancements supporting the operating margin results, specifically investments in automation and process improvements across various functions, including customer support, order processing, and financial reporting.

One final point — we’ve made structural improvements to better enable CapEx, and the CapEx comments for this quarter, primarily allocating around 60% to expanding our manufacturing capacity. This includes investments in upgrading existing fabs to support advanced process nodes and procuring new equipment, such as EUV lithography systems.

Let’s now open the floor for Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. You mentioned gains in the first quarter revenue results. What gives you confidence that these are sustainable?

Alan Reynolds:
We are focused on executing our IDM 2.0 strategy, which includes investing in leading-edge manufacturing capacity, expanding our foundry services business, and developing innovative products that address the evolving needs of our customers.

Analyst 2:
On the Q2 P&L guidance, is this factoring in potential supply chain disruptions?

Sarah Chen:
Yes, we have considered potential supply chain constraints. We project supply chain constraints cost us approximately $30-$40 million in revenue during the quarter.

Analyst 3:
Can you elaborate on early traction with CapEx and related initiatives?

David Lee:
We're seeing positive momentum in our engagement with the European Union regarding the European Chips Act. We anticipate that this initiative will provide significant financial support for our planned expansion in Europe, potentially reducing our net CapEx outlay in the coming years.

Analyst 4:
How are you thinking about long-term opportunity in the customer LTA update with ARM Holdings?

Emily Carter:
The LTA facilitates deeper technical collaboration between our engineering teams and ARM's silicon architects. We are actively engaged in co-development efforts focused on process optimization specifically tailored to ARM's core designs.

Closing

Alan Reynolds:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us. We’re energized by the results this quarter and remain focused on disciplined execution and strategic expansion. Looking forward to sharing continued progress next time.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
